subject: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <security@alphatech.com>, Tom Reynolds <itops@alphatech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions

Hi Maya / Tom —

Great to kick this off. Per our onboarding checklist (attached), I wanted to capture the access-control items we'll need to close in the first 2 weeks so the Redwood Private instance can be fully integrated with your identity + network posture. Short summary and asks below: 

1) SSO / SAML
- Please send your SAML metadata XML (IdP metadata). If you have separate metadata for staging vs prod, include both.
- We recommend an assertion that includes: nameidentifier (persistent), email, givenName, familyName, groups (if available).

2) SCIM provisioning
- High-level SCIM mapping we propose (we'll share a CSV): userName -> user.principalName, givenName, familyName, emails[type=work], groups -> groups.
- Do you require SCIM over HTTPS with client certificate or token-based service account? If token, please share intended rotation cadence and where we should store creds (we support KMS/HSM integrations).

3) IP allowlists and network controls
- Please confirm source CIDR ranges that need access to the Private control plane and API endpoints (staging + prod). If you prefer a VPN or private peering, note that here.

4) Service accounts & least privilege
- For SCIM and operational API actions we suggest two service accounts: scim-provisioner (read/write groups + users) and scim-audit (read-only). Do you have naming or RBAC constraints?

5) Org policies and session controls
- Any specific session timeouts, MFA exceptions, or data residency rules we should reflect in the role mapping/policies?

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_access_checklist.pdf (our checklist + timeline)

Would you be able to respond with the metadata and a copy of your desired SCIM mapping by Tuesday 17 Aug? If helpful we can do a 30-minute SCIM walkthrough with your identity engineer — propose Tue 17 11:00-11:30 PT.

Next steps from our side: Laura will own the SCIM mapping doc and Monica will coordinate the staging window and IP allowlist tests. Vivek will be on call for any infra questions.

Thanks —
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

---
attachment: redwood_onboarding_access_checklist.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Maya Singh <security@alphatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <itops@alphatech.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions

Thanks, Karthik —

Attaching our IdP metadata for prod (alphatech_saml_metadata.xml). Staging metadata is still on our IdP admin; we'll push that to you by EOD tomorrow. A few answers up front: 

- SAML: We provide groups in the assertion under attribute 'memberOf'. We can include persistent NameID. We need Redwood to honor an email_verified claim when present.

- SCIM: Our preference is token-based service account for SCIM. Tokens rotate quarterly; we can provide a long-lived token for the initial onboarding and a rotated token before go-live.

- Network: Control-plane access limited to these CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24 (prod ops), 203.0.113.0/24 (dev/staging). We also require that any service accounts originate from our corporate network (we log source IP).

- Compliance: We have a standard infosec checklist — we will need the standard SOC2 evidence items (audit logs for admin actions, retention policy for logs). Please confirm Redwood's retention defaults and whether we can request an extended retention window.

Questions from our end: 
- For the token-based SCIM account, can Redwood support IP-locking the token so it only works from our CIDR ranges?
- For group mapping, we have nested AD groups; do you support flattening or do you expect us to supply a flat list?

Attaching: alphatech_saml_metadata.xml

Best,
Maya Singh
Head of Security
AlphaTech

---
attachment: alphatech_saml_metadata.xml (application/xml)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <security@alphatech.com>, Tom Reynolds <itops@alphatech.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions

Thanks Maya — very helpful. Replies inline below and next steps at the end.

> We provide groups in the assertion under attribute 'memberOf'. We can include persistent NameID. We need Redwood to honor an email_verified claim when present.

That works. We'll map memberOf -> groups and honor email_verified if present. Can you confirm the exact attribute name (case-sensitive) in the XML export? If it's 'memberOf' we'll map it directly.

> Our preference is token-based service account for SCIM. Tokens rotate quarterly; we can provide a long-lived token for the initial onboarding and a rotated token before go-live.

We support token-based service accounts and can accept an initial token for provisioning. We also support IP-locking tokens at the control-plane level; we'll add the token+CIDR constraint to the scim-provisioner role. Please provide the initial token via a secure channel (we'll send a pre-authenticated upload link).

> Control-plane access limited to these CIDRs: 198.51.100.0/24 (prod ops), 203.0.113.0/24 (dev/staging).

Confirmed. We'll add both ranges. For the API endpoints we'll also ask for any NAT egress ranges if you plan to call Redwood APIs from within your VPC (helps with audit mapping).

> Compliance: need SOC2 evidence (audit logs for admin actions, retention). Please confirm Redwood's retention defaults and possibility of extended retention.

Our default admin audit logs retention is 90 days in the Console with an export option to your S3 for longer retention. We offer a 2-year retention add-on per enterprise contract; Laura can include options in the SOW.

> Question: can Redwood support IP-locking the token so it only works from our CIDR ranges?

Yes — we can lock SCIM tokens to CIDR ranges for Private customers. We'll include scim-provisioner token binding to 198.51.100.0/24 and 203.0.113.0/24 as requested.

> Nested AD groups — do you support flattening?

We offer both options: inbound flattening (Redwood will flatten nested groups to membership list) or we can accept a pre-flattened attribute. Laura will produce two sample mapping variants in the CSV: flattened and nested (with path notation).

Proposed next steps (we can action in parallel):
- Laura: share alphatech_scim_group_map.csv with concrete examples (today).
- Monica: schedule staging SCIM sync window Tue 17 14:00-15:00 PT (suggested).
- Karthik/Vivek: we will request the initial SCIM token via secure upload and configure IP-locking.

I'll block the 17 Aug 14:00 slot for a 30-minute provisioning test. If that time doesn't work please let us know.

Thanks —
Karthik

---
attachment: alphatech_scim_group_map.csv (text/csv)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Singh <security@alphatech.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Tom Reynolds <itops@alphatech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Aug 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions

Quick operational notes from the implementation team: 

1) Staging vs Prod endpoints: We will set up two endpoints: https://private-staging.redwood.alpha/ALT and https://private-prod.redwood.alpha/ALT. SCIM provisioning will be enabled against staging first.

2) Suggestion for least-privileged service accounts:
- scim-provisioner (scim:users:write, scim:groups:write) — IP-locked to 203.0.113.0/24 for staging and 198.51.100.0/24 for prod.
- scim-audit (scim:users:read, scim:groups:read) — read-only; recommended for scheduled compliance exports.

3) Org policy recommendation: we typically apply 'require_admin_acceptance_for_third_party_apps' and enforce session timeout of 12 hours for console sessions. If you have a different standard, we can adopt it.

4) SCIM testing: we'll perform a sandbox sync to validate group mapping; we recommend enabling dry-run mode (no writes) first, then small-batch writes.

I'll own the mapping CSV and will attach an example mapping (flattened vs nested) — Laura

Best,
Laura Bennett
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Reynolds <itops@alphatech.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@alphatech.com, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Aug 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AlphaTech onboarding: access control plan & SCIM mapping questions

All good from our side. Confirming the staging window for Tue 17 Aug 14:00 PT worked for the small sync — looks good. A couple of follow-ups: 

- Please provide the DocuSign link for the SOW — our legal needs the signed SOW before enabling production access.
- For the SCIM token upload: prefer a secure form or pre-auth URL. We will rotate the token after go-live; give us the process to rotate without downtime.
- We'll want a 2-hour canary deployment in prod (small target group) before full cutover.

Can you add the DocuSign link and the rotation-runbook to the shared onboarding page? Once we have those, we can finalize the timeline and sign.

Thanks,
Tom Reynolds
IT Operations Manager
AlphaTech
